When a user double-taps the Shift key, the daemon intercepts the system event, immediately querying the active Accessibility API to extract the currently focused text buffer or highlighted selection. This avoids the resource-heavy overhead of maintaining a persistent DOM or running an embedded browser engine. By utilizing direct system calls for clipboard management and file serialization, the utility writes out pure Markdown payloads to a designated local directory instantaneously. The memory footprint remains remarkably low, hovering well under twenty megabytes during idle states, and spikes negligibly during string extraction. Because there is no client-server synchronization loop, data never leaves the local machine, guaranteeing absolute privacy and eliminating network latency entirely from the critical path. The entire execution pipeline from keypress to disk write executes within single-digit milliseconds, offering a seamless, non-blocking asynchronous user experience that feels natively integrated into the operating system shell environment.
